title: Customer Relations Guideline: Goodwill Relief on Kestrel Auto Finance Late Fees
content:
**Guideline.** Goodwill relief on a late fee charged on Kestrel Auto Finance Retail Installment Contracts is posted as a principal credit recorded as a billing correction that names the late-fee entry, and it does not count as a payment toward any due date. Goodwill relief is given only while the goodwill reliefs on the contract dated fewer than 12 whole months before the request date, counting every waived late fee and every billing-correction principal credit on the contract as a goodwill relief, are below the tier's late fee waivers per 12 months. The goodwill credit is the full amount of the most recent late fee charged on the contract, rounded to the cent. It is never below zero and never above that late fee.

## Allowance by tier

| Tier | Late fee waivers per 12 months | Relief possible when the reliefs counted are |
|---|---|---|
| Kestrel Finance Tier E | 0 | never |
| Kestrel Finance Tier D | 1 | 0 |
| Kestrel Finance Tier C | 1 | 0 |
| Kestrel Finance Tier B | 1 | 0 |
| Kestrel Finance Tier A | 2 | 0 or 1 |
| Kestrel Finance Tier A+ | 2 | 0 or 1 |

## What counts as a goodwill relief

Every waived late fee and every billing-correction principal credit on the contract, each counted when fewer than 12 whole months separate its date from the request date. Hypothetical, request on 2026-09-14: a billing-correction credit dated 2025-09-15 is 11 whole months back and counts; one dated 2025-09-14 is 12 whole months back and does not.

## Hypothetical cases

- Tier B, no relief in the window, most recent late fee 24.00: relief is given, and the goodwill credit is 24.00, booked as a billing correction naming that late-fee entry.
- Tier B, one waived late fee 7 whole months back: 1 is not below 1, so no relief is given.
- Tier A, one billing-correction credit 3 whole months back: 1 is below 2, so relief is given.
- Tier E: the allowance is 0, so no goodwill relief is given.
